entry.title: Initia hack drove its USDC bridge reserve down to $63 as withdrawals failed
entry.summary:
Initia suffered a bridge exploit on October 23 that drained its USDC bridge reserve down to $63, with users unable to complete withdrawals. Reporting on the incident states roughly $3 million in real assets exited through bridges against $7 million in unbacked balances.
The reserve depletion left the bridge unable to honor user withdrawals, turning a protocol security breach into a direct loss of access for holders who relied on the bridge to move USDC on and off Initia.
The reported gap between the ~$3 million in real assets that left through bridges and the $7 million in unbacked balances indicates the shortfall exceeds the value actually withdrawn. The incident reduced the USDC bridge reserve to $63.

entry.title: AI agents help rescue ETH’s Glamsterdam fork, ‘Steal My Bitcoin’ site: Hodler’s Digest
entry.summary:
Ethereum's second and final Glamsterdam hard fork testnet on Hoodi was cancelled this week after ChainSecurity found vulnerabilities in the gas-scaling EIPs 8037 and 8038 that could break at least 13 DeFi contracts when a call runs out of gas. Researchers at Eth Labs and the Ethereum Foundation independently spun up AI agents to scan contracts for the flaws, then set up a shared message board in the form of a GitHub repo to coordinate the agents' work.
The cancellation postpones the dress rehearsal for an upgrade that Ethereum DeFi operators depend on, and Eth Labs' Derek Chiang said protocols designers should in future do "much more thorough analysis of potential breakages" much earlier in the process. He added that the agent exercise proved effective enough that a second board has been opened to study EIP-8198, or "Quick Slots", proposed for the follow-up Hegota fork.
Chiang said the vulnerability was found "a few minutes to midnight," causing everyone to scramble, and the Hoodi testnet is not expected to be rescheduled until all of the fork's second-order effects have been properly analyzed. He likened the setup to the OpenAI–Hugging Face hack, where rogue agents coordinated through a message board, noting "the same pattern is useful for the good agents too."

entry.title: Crypto Exchange First Called It a “False Alarm,” Then Admitted to a $16 Million Loss
entry.summary:
A cryptocurrency exchange initially dismissed a security incident as a false alarm before later acknowledging that it had suffered a $16 million loss, according to Koin Bülteni. The exchange was not identified in the report, and no timeline or technical details of the incident were disclosed.
The reversal from denial to confirmed loss puts the focus on how exchanges communicate during incidents, since initial statements shape how users judge whether their funds are at risk.
The reported loss figure is $16 million. The report does not name the exchange or specify whether user funds, corporate funds or a hot wallet were affected.

entry.title: Hyperliquid to List 11 Tokenized US Stocks and ETFs for Spot Trading, Opening Tomorrow
entry.summary:
Hyperliquid will list 11 USDC-denominated HIP-1 spot markets for tokenized US stocks and ETFs issued by EQX Labs, covering S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 trackers (EQSPY, EQQQQ) plus single-name exposure to Nvidia, Tesla, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Micron and SpaceX. The tokens are already registered on Hyperliquid mainnet, but matching will not open until 21:30 Beijing time on October 26 (9:30 a.m. ET the same day).
The listing adds a tokenized-equity asset class to one of the largest on-chain derivatives venues, extending on-chain trading in major US stocks and index trackers beyond conventional market hours. Trading has not yet begun, so liquidity and any regulatory response remain untested.
EQX says each token is backed 1:1 by real shares but is legally structured as a limited-recourse debt note issued by a segregated portfolio company in the British Virgin Islands rather than direct share ownership, and is not offered to US persons.

entry.title: Paradigm CTO: New EVM With Built-in JIT Compilation Has Completed Audit
entry.summary:
Paradigm partner and CTO Georgios Konstantopoulos said on X that the team is about to release an audited EVM with built-in just-in-time (JIT) compilation, named evm2, whose code is already public on GitHub. evm2 is a Rust EVM implementation that lets developers customize opcodes, gas rules, transaction types and precompiles without modifying core code, and its README claims execution speeds of up to 2x the current mainstream Rust EVM, revm.
According to Konstantopoulos, evm2 is slated for use in Foundry, Reth, Tempo and other EVM ecosystem projects that adopt Paradigm's tech stack — three components that currently all run on revm.
The audit is described as complete, but the release is framed as upcoming rather than shipped. The 2x speed figure is a claim from the repository's README rather than an independently verified benchmark.

entry.title: Kraken’s token delisting gives holders until Jan. 29 to withdraw 13 assets
entry.summary:
Kraken is delisting 13 assets and has set January 29 as the deadline for holders to withdraw those tokens from the exchange. The move removes the affected tokens from Kraken's tradable lineup.
Holders of the 13 affected assets have a fixed window ending January 29 to move their tokens off Kraken; after that deadline the exchange's delisting process governs what happens to remaining balances.
The delisting covers 13 assets specifically, not a platform-wide change, and the January 29 withdrawal deadline is the operative date for affected holders.

entry.title: Keystone customers say breach exposed data the hardware wallet maker promised to delete
entry.summary:
Customers of hardware wallet maker Keystone say a data breach exposed personal information that the company had previously pledged to delete, according to a report by The Block published on Oct. 25, 2026. The accounts describe a leak of customer records rather than of wallet keys or on-device funds.
The exposure creates phishing and physical-security risk for self-custody users, whose contact and delivery information can be used to target them directly, according to the report. It also undercuts a data-retention promise made by a vendor whose product is built around user-controlled security.
The complaint centers on data that customers say Keystone had told them would be erased, and the reported material relates to customer contact and shipping details rather than the air-gapped signing devices themselves.

entry.title: Coinbase Founder Brian Armstrong Gained Majority Voting Control Without Buying More Than Half the Company
entry.summary:
Coinbase founder Brian Armstrong has gained majority voting control of the company through its share structure even though he owns less than half of its equity, according to Coinpaper.
It means control of Coinbase's corporate decisions is concentrated in its founder despite his minority economic stake.
The control is attributed to Coinbase's share structure rather than additional purchases; dual-class arrangements commonly separate economic ownership from voting rights by assigning different votes per share.

entry.title: Stablecoin Payments Scale Up: Coinbase-Thunes Partnership
entry.summary:
Coinbase and Thunes are partnering to scale stablecoin-based cross-border payments, according to a OneSafe.io analysis, extending institutional use of stablecoins for settlement.
The partnership is intended to expand institutional use of stablecoins for cross-border settlement, according to the report.
Thunes provides cross-border payment solutions through multiple channels and payment options.

entry.title: Hong Kong’s Biggest Bank Puts a Stablecoin in 3 Million Wallets
entry.summary:
HSBC launched RedCoin (ticker RCHKD), a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin licensed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, on its PayMe app, with more than 3.3 million users able to activate wallets in the coming days to send money to friends or pay at over 100,000 PayMe merchants. The bank said it plans to add the token to its HSBC HK Mobile Banking app later this year.
The launch puts an HKMA-licensed stablecoin inside a major global bank's existing consumer wallet, letting Hong Kong users pay with blockchain-based money without opening a crypto exchange — a step beyond the trading-platform venues where stablecoins have mostly circulated.
RedCoin runs on HSBC's own private ledger rather than a public blockchain such as Ethereum, and balances cannot move between PayMe and HSBC's banking app; it is also not a bank deposit and is not covered by Hong Kong's Deposit Protection Scheme. HSBC's reserve tracker showed roughly $10.2 million of RedCoin circulating shortly after launch, backed by $10.4 million held entirely in cash, with the first independent attestation of reserves expected after the fourth quarter of 2026. John O'Neill, HSBC's managing director of digital assets and currencies, said the bank will "soon add more products, including expanding into wholesale corporate and institutional use cases."

entry.title: Initia Discloses Attack Details: MoveVM Caching Vulnerability Led to About $2.7 Million Being Moved Out
entry.summary:
Initia said in a post on X that an attacker exploited a MoveVM script-caching vulnerability at 22:59 on October 23 to bypass security checks and forge MoveVM state, crediting itself with WETH, iUSD and USDC that had no actual backing. Roughly $2.7 million in assets had already been moved out before the network was paused.
The incident prompted Initia to pause its L1 and Rollups, halting activity across the ecosystem while the fix is completed and audited; asset recovery work is ongoing with security partners.
Initia said the total supply of the affected tokens did not change and that INIT was not minted, so its total supply is unaffected. The funds moved were 105 WETH and about 1.4 million AUSD0 via LayerZero, plus about 1.08 million USDC via Noble and CCTP, later swapped into 1,135.52 ETH now held at Ethereum address 0x358ef0130f7a5aa516dcd81bdc80b18cde41cac8.

entry.title: Crypto longs lose $404 million in four hours as bitcoin briefly slips below $80,000
entry.summary:
Bitcoin briefly traded below $80,000, triggering $404 million in liquidations of crypto long positions within a four-hour window, according to The Block. The move wiped out leveraged bullish bets as the price dipped under the $80,000 level before recovering.
The scale of the four-hour liquidation total indicates that a large volume of leveraged long positions had been built up near the $80,000 level, and their forced closure amplified the downward move.
The liquidation figure covers long positions only, over a four-hour window, and the sub-$80,000 break is described as brief. No exchange failure, insolvency or protocol-level disruption was reported alongside the deleveraging.

entry.title: NYSE’s owner is backing 24/7 stock tokens without Wall Street’s usual price rules
entry.summary:
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is backing round-the-clock trading of tokenized stocks that would operate outside Wall Street's conventional price-control rules, according to CryptoSlate. The report describes 24/7 trading of on-chain equity tokens that sidesteps the traditional price-band and circuit-breaker regime applied to US equities.
The backing of a major exchange operator gives weight to the idea of round-the-clock, on-chain equity trading outside standard market-protection rules. Concrete impact is not yet established, as no launch scope, partners, or regulatory approvals were detailed in the available reporting.
The model described would operate without the price-band and circuit-breaker controls that normally apply to US equity trading. The reporting provided does not specify which tokens, venues, or jurisdictions would be involved, nor whether any regulatory approval has been sought or granted.

entry.title: X100 Exploit Nets 4.85 Million USDT After Governance Takeover
entry.summary:
X100, a DeFi protocol, was exploited for 4.85 million USDT after attackers gained control of its governance, according to The Defiant. The governance takeover allowed the attackers to move funds out of the protocol.
The loss is a direct hit to X100's users and liquidity providers, and it shows that governance control, not only contract bugs, can be the path through which a protocol's funds are drained.
The stolen amount is denominated in USDT and totals 4.85 million. The attack vector is described as a takeover of the protocol's governance rather than an external contract exploit.

entry.title: Swell Pauses swETH and rswETH Deposits and Withdrawals Amid Abnormally High Cont
entry.summary:
Ethereum staking protocol Swell has paused deposits and withdrawals for its swETH and rswETH tokens until it corrects the tokens' net asset values and exchange rates. Data showed the swETH and rswETH contracts reporting exchange rates of roughly 1.203 ETH and 1.138 ETH respectively — about 6% and 5% above normal levels.
On-chain analyst Spreek suspected a compromise of the tokens' admin keys and identified a malicious upgrade contract that could affect around 2,500 ETH, which has not yet been executed. Halting deposits and withdrawals means holders of both tokens temporarily cannot redeem them through the protocol.
Swell said no ETH has been transferred out of the affected contracts and that the exact cause remains under investigation. The suspected malicious upgrade had not been executed at the time of reporting.

entry.title: Franklin Templeton Adds ~$150 Million in Tokenized Fund Shares to XRP Ledger, All Concentrated in a Single Wallet
entry.summary:
Franklin Templeton added roughly $150 million of tokenized money-market fund shares to the XRP Ledger, lifting the network's sgBENJI supply from about 48 million to 193 million tokens, according to CoinDesk. Priced at $1.039 per share in the transaction records, the total is worth about $200 million and is held in a single wallet.
The move nearly quadruples the fund's footprint on XRP Ledger, extending a large U.S. asset manager's tokenized money-market product onto a public chain beyond its original Stellar base.
The tokens are all concentrated in one wallet, a holding pattern the reports note without attributing it to a specific custodian or client. Franklin Templeton's BENJI was the first U.S.-registered money market fund to use a public blockchain as its system of record, and sgBENJI is tracked as a tokenized fund asset by RWA.xyz.

entry.title: Circle’s new USDC auctions let institutions collect the fees others pay to cash out
entry.summary:
Circle introduced USDC auctions that let institutional holders provide or bid for exit liquidity and earn the fees paid by others cashing out.
The mechanism gives institutional holders a way to earn fees by supplying exit liquidity for USDC cash-outs, adding a fee-earning role alongside existing redemption channels.
Auction participants can take either side—supplying exit liquidity or bidding for it—while the fees paid by users cashing out go to the liquidity providers.

entry.title: Electrum Patches Wallet Flaw Exploited Through Malicious Servers
entry.summary:
Electrum has patched a vulnerability in its Bitcoin wallet that attackers exploited by directing users to malicious servers, The Defiant reported. The fix closes a flaw in the open-source wallet that could be reached through the server connections the client relies on.
Electrum is one of the longest-running and most widely used Bitcoin wallets, so a flaw reachable through server connections affects a broad base of self-custody users who hold their own keys.
The exploit path runs through Electrum's links to third-party servers rather than the Bitcoin network itself; such servers can push custom text and popups into the wallet interface.

entry.title: Swell Pauses swETH and rswETH Deposits and Withdrawals
entry.summary:
Swell, a liquid staking and restaking protocol, has suspended deposits and withdrawals for its swETH liquid staking token and rswETH liquid restaking token, saying it is working with security partners and SEAL 911 to fully remediate its infrastructure. The team said its next step is to restore NAV (net asset value) to the correct level, after which it will reopen deposits and withdrawals.
Suspending both deposits and withdrawals freezes user exit paths, leaving holders of swETH and rswETH unable to redeem on the protocol while the issue is investigated. Swell stated that all user funds are safe.
Swell said the day before that it had noticed reports of suspicious activity involving the swETH and rswETH contracts. The team warned that phishing attacks tend to increase during such incidents and urged users to rely only on official channels.

entry.title: Aave changes USDT borrowing rules and loan costs suddenly jump
entry.summary:
Aave changed its USDT borrowing rules, and borrowing costs on the protocol rose sharply as a result, CryptoSlate reported.
The adjustment directly changes the cost of carrying USDT-denominated debt on one of DeFi's largest lending protocols, affecting borrowers who rely on stablecoin liquidity.

entry.title: Succinct Patches SP1 Bug That Could Let Invalid Proofs Pass
entry.summary:
Succinct patched a soundness vulnerability in its SP1 zero-knowledge virtual machine (zkVM) that could have allowed invalid zero-knowledge proofs to be accepted as valid, according to The Defiant.
A soundness flaw in a proving system breaks the core guarantee that an accepted proof corresponds to correct computation, so any system relying on SP1 proofs to validate state transitions would inherit that risk.
SP1 is Succinct's open-source zkVM that verifies the execution of programs written in Rust or other LLVM-compiled languages. The specific version affected, the discovery timeline and the patch details were not disclosed in the available material.

entry.title: Lido launches 0x02 CSM, allowing node operators to run 0x02 validators permissionlessly
entry.summary:
Lido has launched 0x02 CSM, a module that lets node operators permissionlessly run 0x02 validators with an effective balance of up to 2,048 ETH through the Lido protocol. Operators do not need to supply the full stake themselves: they post a bond of 32 ETH for the first validator key and 30 ETH for each additional key, with the remaining stake allocated by Lido.
Once a validator reaches the 2,048 ETH effective balance, Lido says operators' capital multiplier comes to roughly 2.18x to 2.26x compared with solo staking. The module's initial stake share is capped at 0.01% of Lido Core TVL, about 32 validator keys, with capacity to be expanded gradually.
The existing 0x01 CSM continues to run in parallel, and current operators do not need to switch to the new module.

entry.title: Morning Minute: a16z Drops 'Crypto' From Its Fund
entry.summary:
Andreessen Horowitz is renaming its crypto fund "a16z Frontier" and broadening its mandate to cover AI, autonomous machines and biology, while saying it will continue investing in crypto. Chris Dixon, who has led the crypto team since 2018, runs the new fund alongside Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet.
The firm describes the change as "an expansion" rather than a retreat from crypto, but a fund that was crypto-only will now weigh crypto deals against AI, autonomous machines and biology in the same partner meeting. Dixon's stated rationale is that blockchains have faded into the background of products shipped by Wall Street and fintech firms, so companies should be judged by what they build rather than the underlying plumbing.
The most recent fund size on record is $2.2 billion, announced in May. Dixon has said crypto retains a role in the new mandate — enabling AI agents to pay each other — and points to Oculus, Skydio and Zipline as models for long-horizon bets.

entry.title: CoinDCX belatedly admits latest hack; Ireland fines Coinbase anew
entry.summary:
Indian crypto exchange CoinDCX has acknowledged a new security breach, confirming the incident only after the fact rather than at the time it occurred. Separately, Ireland's central bank issued another penalty against Coinbase's Irish entity, with reports citing a €3.25 million ($3.6 million) fine over safeguarding and outsourcing obligations.
The two disclosures land on the same exchange-risk themes — custody security and regulatory compliance — that supervisors have been tightening. Ireland's central bank framed the Coinbase action as customer protection, stating: "This action against Coinbase Ireland underlines the Central Bank's focus on ensuring that customers are at all times protected and that the integrity of the financial system is maintained."
The Coinbase penalty reported in the safeguarding and outsourcing case requires approval from Ireland's High Court before taking effect. Delano separately reported a €21.5 million penalty against Coinbase Europe for anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing failures, described as Ireland's first enforcement action in the crypto sector.

entry.title: Bitcoin ETFs shed $635 million as BTC tests their holdings’ estimated $81,500 cost basis
entry.summary:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $635 million in net outflows as bitcoin traded near the estimated aggregate cost basis of ETF holdings, put at roughly $81,500, according to CryptoSlate. The cost-basis level is an estimate for the whole issuer cohort rather than a disclosed figure from any single fund.
The aggregate cost basis of the spot ETF cohort is the level that indicates whether the marginal ETF holder is in profit or loss; when spot trades above it, ETF flows have tended to be stickier, according to market commentary compiled by The Bitcoin Layer. Trading at or below that level puts the flow dynamic under pressure.
The $81,500 figure is an estimate derived from combining daily net flow data with live pricing across major spot ETF products, as described by ETF tracking tools such as On-Chain Mind. Estimates of the cohort's aggregate cost basis vary by provider and by the date on which they are computed.

entry.title: Wells Fargo, Arm and 22 Companies Object to Their Tokenized Stocks Trading on OKXICE Platform
entry.summary:
According to a regulatory filing seen by Reuters, six more companies — including Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit — have joined the list of issuers refusing to allow their shares to be tokenized on OKXICE, the joint tokenized-stock venue proposed by OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). The filing shows 22 companies in total have now objected to the project.
The objections add to corporate resistance facing equity tokenization even after US securities regulators recently approved such products, and the filing does not state the companies' specific reasons for objecting.
Sixteen of the objecting companies are listed on Nasdaq and six on the NYSE, with Microsoft and Alphabet among those that objected in the prior week. OKXICE co-chair and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo said the venture expected more objections, and the project had initially proposed 62 companies for tokenized listings when it filed with the SEC earlier in October.

entry.title: ⚡️Kalshi plans December launch of futures tracking US CPI and core inflation
entry.summary:
Kalshi is pitching large global banks and hedge funds on a December launch of exchange-traded futures tracking US CPI and core inflation, according to Bloomberg, and has hired former Barclays trader Michael Ashton to design the contracts and bring in institutional investors. A Kalshi spokesperson confirmed the company is developing CPI futures but did not disclose launch details.
According to the report, the product would be the only futures contract currently tied directly to CPI, after CME Group stopped offering its own CPI futures.
Per pitch documents seen by Bloomberg, the futures would cover the next 12 reference months, followed by May and November contracts for the following four years, trade 24 hours a day from Sunday to Friday, and be cleared by Kalshi Klear. Ashton, hired to design the contracts, is known for his inflation trading expertise and has been dubbed "Mr. Inflation."

entry.title: Solana’s biggest network change since 2020 is live. Here’s how users benefit
entry.summary:
Solana activated its Alpenglow consensus overhaul on mainnet, replacing the TowerBFT consensus mechanism with Votor and the Turbine block-propagation protocol with Rotor. The change cuts block finality from roughly 12.8 seconds to about 150 milliseconds.
According to Solana, Alpenglow is the network's first major consensus replacement since TowerBFT, changing how validators vote and how blocks reach finality. A finality time of roughly 150 milliseconds instead of about 12.8 seconds directly shortens the wait for transaction confirmation on the network.
Solana states the upgrade leaves transaction execution and the SVM unchanged, altering only consensus-related mechanics and how consensus information is exposed to downstream infrastructure. Rotor, like Turbine, erasure-codes each block into smaller "shreds" that can be reconstructed from a subset.

entry.title: Morpho Supports Borrowing Stablecoins Against Robinhood Stock Tokens as Collateral
entry.summary:
Morpho announced on October 22 that Robinhood stock tokens are now live on its platform, allowing users to post tokenized equities as collateral and borrow stablecoins against them. Morpho supplies the underlying credit network while Robinhood Chain provides the tokenization infrastructure, and any application can integrate the resulting lending markets.
The integration extends on-chain credit markets to tokenized equity collateral, a step beyond the crypto-native assets that typically back DeFi loans.
Morpho positions itself as the credit layer rather than the tokenization layer, leaving issuance and settlement of the stock tokens to Robinhood Chain. The announcement did not specify which equities are supported, collateral ratios, or which applications have integrated the markets.

entry.title: Uniswap Aggregator Hooks Go Live, Wrapping External Liquidity Sources Into v4 Pools
entry.summary:
Uniswap Labs said in an Oct. 22 post that Aggregator Hooks are now live, making Uniswap v4 function as an aggregator by wrapping external liquidity sources into v4 pools that any router can treat as a Uniswap pool. The feature is available in the Uniswap Web app and API on Ethereum mainnet, Base and Robinhood Chain, with more chains to follow and seven liquidity sources at launch, including Curve, Fluid and PancakeSwap.
Uniswap said most onchain liquidity already sits on Uniswap but new liquidity can still emerge elsewhere, so folding external venues into v4 puts it in more direct competition with standalone DEX aggregators. Swaps routed through those external sources pay the protocol fee and contribute to UNI burn, linking aggregator volume to UNI supply.
Per block, the router pulls the latest quotes from integrated sources, builds the best path between Uniswap pools and external venues, and settles within a single transaction without requiring new approvals. BlockBeats reported the launch on Oct. 22.

entry.title: SoFi launches interest-bearing, FDIC-insured tokenized deposit for crypto users
entry.summary:
SoFi Technologies on Thursday launched SoFi Earn (ticker SOFIE), a tokenized deposit issued by SoFi Bank that pays a variable 4.40% annual percentage yield, carries no minimum balance requirement, and qualifies for FDIC coverage up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category. SoFi describes it as the first tokenized deposit offered directly to consumers by a US national bank and expects the rollout to SoFi Crypto members to be completed in November.
Each SOFIE corresponds to $1 on deposit at SoFi Bank and can be converted one-for-one into SoFiUSD, the bank's dollar-pegged stablecoin, to buy crypto in the app or send to supported external wallets — giving crypto users a bank-backed, deposit-insured way to hold idle dollars before they are deployed.
SOFIE deposits continue to earn interest until they are converted, whereas SoFiUSD itself, like other stablecoins, is not an FDIC-insured deposit. Members reach the separate SOFIE deposit account through their SoFi Crypto account.

entry.title: CoinDCX Responds Again to Unaccounted $15.8 Million in User Deposits: Deprecated Address Was Long Abandoned, Operational Losses Borne by Platform
entry.summary:
On Oct. 22, India-based exchange CoinDCX again addressed on-chain controversy over deposit address TQKJQ, saying the address was compromised and deprecated after its July 2025 security incident and that users kept sending funds to it anyway. The exchange said its routine sweep process failed for a period, the failure was discovered that morning, and the resulting operational losses will be absorbed by CoinDCX, while all affected deposits were credited to users.
CoinDCX says affected users were fully credited and that funds remain in segregated cold wallets, with no loss of platform funds in active wallets — limiting direct user impact from an incident it otherwise describes as an operational failure.
The exchange said current centralized and user addresses are unaffected and that trading and platform operations continue as normal. It did not detail how roughly $15.8 million went unaccounted for over an extended period.

entry.title: OKX UAE Launches Tokenised US Stocks with 24/7 Trading on VARA Licence
entry.summary:
OKX's UAE entity has launched tokenised US stock trading that is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, operating under its licence from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA). The offering extends regulated, crypto-style market access to US equity exposure.
A VARA-licensed venue offering round-the-clock tokenised equity exposure widens access to tokenised securities in one of the crypto industry's more developed regulatory jurisdictions, putting equity exposure on the same always-on footing as crypto trading.
Tokenised stocks are blockchain-based tokens designed to reflect the value of a specific equity. Separate reporting on OKX's broader tokenised-equity plans describes trading against stablecoins including USDC, USDG and USDT through permissioned Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on XLayer, OKX's layer-2 blockchain.

entry.title: polkadotfoundationwarnsfearlesswalletextensionleakedprivatekeys
entry.summary:
The Polkadot Foundation issued a warning that the Fearless Wallet browser extension leaked users' private keys, leaving affected wallets exposed to compromise. The warning names the third-party Polkadot-ecosystem wallet directly.
Private keys are what authorize transfers from a wallet, so anyone holding a leaked key can move the associated funds without further approval from the owner.
Fearless Wallet's browser extension is built for the Kusama and Polkadot networks and distributed through the Chrome Web Store for Chrome and Chromium-based browsers. The warning as reported did not include confirmed loss figures, exploit scale, or the number of affected users.

entry.title: Dune launches real-time data feeds covering 200 onchain trading venues
entry.summary:
Dune announced on Thursday that it has launched real-time market data feeds covering more than 200 onchain trading venues across 12 blockchains, including Ethereum, Solana, Base and XLayer, delivering trade data roughly one second after execution. The feeds cover spot trading on decentralized exchanges as well as perpetual futures on Hyperliquid and Lighter, with standardized data on prices, trade sizes and transaction details.
Dune co-founder and CEO Fredrik Haga said most institutions are watching onchain markets first because "they can't price these assets properly without them anymore," pointing to market data as the entry point for institutional onchain participation. The launch comes as tokenized stock markets expand and face growing scrutiny.
Haga said quant funds, market makers, asset managers and bank trading desks are among the first clients, but declined to identify them, citing nondisclosure agreements. According to Dune, these firms use the data to assess liquidity, compare prices across venues and evaluate trading strategies before committing capital.

entry.title: a16z Drops Crypto From Its Name, Widens Bets to AI and Frontier Tech
entry.summary:
Andreessen Horowitz is renaming its crypto fund "a16z Crypto" to "a16z Frontier," widening its mandate to AI, biology, hardware and other long-horizon technologies while saying it will keep investing in crypto and advocating for crypto regulation. The change was disclosed in an email to the firm's newsletter subscribers on Thursday, with Chris Dixon leading the fund alongside Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet.
a16z is among the largest backers of the crypto industry, and as the report frames it, a firm of that size dropping "crypto" from its name shows where it may expect the next wave of capital to go.
The firm calls the move "an expansion" and says crypto stays: "we will continue to invest in crypto and related ventures and advocate for sensible crypto regulation." The post gave no size for the renamed fund; the latest figure on record is the $2.2 billion announced in May.

entry.title: Solana's new consensus protocol Alpenglow goes live on mainnet
entry.summary:
Anza announced that Alpenglow, Solana's new consensus protocol, is now live on mainnet-beta, retiring TowerBFT. The switchover took place at genesis slot 459,653,000, activated at epoch 1064, with 654 validators participating and a handoff that took 900 milliseconds, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds.
The change targets finality — the point at which a transaction can no longer be reversed and the moment an exchange, bank or merchant waits for before treating an asset as moved. Anza CEO Brennan Watt called it "the largest, most ambitious blockchain upgrade since 'The Merge,'" saying the team took it from white paper to mainnet in under 18 months.
Validators approved the upgrade in September 2025, voting 98% in favor of SIMD-0236, the implementing proposal; Anza shipped the protocol in Agave, its validator client, and independent operators coordinated a shared handoff point on the running network while carrying the existing ledger forward. The design is intended to keep working with less than 20% of stake acting maliciously and a further 20% offline, gradually lengthening block times if the network goes 10 seconds without finalizing a block.

entry.title: Binance launches bStocks tokenized securities with 24/7 access
entry.summary:
Binance has launched bStocks, a tokenized securities product that gives users round-the-clock access to tokenized equity exposure on the exchange. The tokens trade on Binance's spot market rather than during traditional stock-market hours.
The product places continuous equity exposure on one of the largest crypto exchanges, extending trading past traditional market hours and creating an instrument that sits between crypto spot markets and regulated securities.
Binance's own documentation states that each bStocks token is backed 1:1 by a US share held at a regulated custodian and is traded 24/7 on the exchange's spot market. The offering is positioned with zero conversion fees and dividend-related features such as automatic reinvestment.

entry.title: Polkadot Community Foundation: Fearless Wallet browser extension contains code that leaks private keys, users must move assets immediately
entry.summary:
The Polkadot Community Foundation posted a security warning on the Polkadot forum stating that versions 3.0.1, 3.0.3, 3.0.4 and 3.0.5 of Fearless Wallet's browser extension contain malicious code that sends users' private keys to attacker-controlled servers when the wallet is unlocked. The code entered the extension's public source in a large commit labeled "TON ecosystem" on February 19, 2025, activated intermittently between February 2025 and October 10, 2026, and can reportedly be reactivated at any time.
The Foundation advises that anyone who used the extension since February 2025 treat every account in it as compromised, generate new key pairs in another wallet and move assets immediately, noting that changing the password or reinstalling the extension is not sufficient. Eight users have so far reported unauthorized transactions attributable to the incident, totaling 17,286 DOT.
The Chrome version is confirmed affected, and a delisted Firefox version used the same code; no such code was found in the Android or iOS mobile apps, though any private key previously imported into the browser extension should still be considered leaked. Users whose assets are staked, in nomination pools, or locked in governance votes can first seek help through PAPI Rescue, a tool developed by the polkadot-api team.

entry.title: Bitcoin Lightning developers sound alarm over security flaws as second patch lands in five days
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Lightning developers are warning publicly about security flaws after a second patch was released within five days, CryptoSlate reported. No confirmed large-scale exploit or systemic loss event has been reported in the available material.
The warning puts Lightning node operators on notice to apply the latest fixes, since security defects in payment-channel software are an operational risk for systems that hold and route funds.
The second patch arrived within a five-day window, underscoring that fixes are being rolled out in quick succession. The available evidence does not establish that the flaws were exploited at scale.
